title: Perfect Investigation
verdict: Every lie answered, down to the tablets he never destroyed.
narrative: You lay it out for {accused} across the library table: the bank's letter, the sixty tablets, the glovebox, the cup he poured himself. He puts his spectacles on to read the bottle's label, as if it might have changed.
He confesses before the inquest opens. Twenty-two years of borrowing from the trust, and one afternoon to stop a man from looking.
Lady Constance keeps the Hall. Agnes Mora gets the legacy the Colonel forgot, from the widow's own pocket. Silas Brook stops cutting foxgloves for the house.

title: True Criminal
verdict: The right name, and enough to hold it.
narrative: {accused} is charged on the morning of the inquest.
The case holds, though his counsel makes much of the statements you never broke and the trust you never followed.
He is convicted at the autumn assizes. The Ashcombe trust is found to be £41,000 short.

title: Wrong Suspect
verdict: A careful case, built around the wrong person.
narrative: Your case against {accused} has a motive, a lie and a moment on the timeline. It is still wrong.
The charges fall at the inquest. By then a set of trust ledgers has quietly been rewritten.
The file is reopened in the winter and handed to someone else.

title: Innocent Person Accused
verdict: An arrest on a hunch, at a family's worst moment.
narrative: {accused} is taken from Ashcombe Hall in a police car while the whole village watches from the Arms.
The charges are dropped a week later. The village does not forget.
Gerald Ashcombe's killer goes on handling the family's affairs for another eleven years.

title: Criminal Escapes
verdict: A cup of tea, and nobody to answer for it.
narrative: The inquest returns an open verdict. Death by digoxin, source unknown.
Whoever poured that cup knew exactly how little you would bring to the coroner.
Case #051 is filed under Unsolved. The foxgloves come up again the next summer, as they always do.
